title: transparent-kv-preservation-during-regional-evacuation-and-staged-traffic-taper
author: Sofia Alvarez
release_notes: Adds a transparent KV preservation layer to reduce cold-start latency during regional evacuations and introduces a staged traffic taper controller to smooth failover-induced load spikes.
description: Motivation: During a regional evacuation we observed large latency spikes and downstream request failures caused by aggressive node drain that evicted per-tenant KV caches and caused many cold KV miss penalties when traffic moved to new regions. This PR implements a transparent KV preservation mechanism that snapshots hot KV entries for tenants that are being evacuated and rehydrates them on target nodes, combined with a staged traffic taper controller that gradually shifts traffic away from the source region to avoid simultaneous cache storms. Design goals: 1) preserve correctness (no tenant-visible state changes), 2) minimize additional cross-region bandwidth, 3) be tolerant to partial failures (fall back to standard evacuation if preservation fails), 4) observable (telemetry for preservation success rate, rehydrate latency, and taper progression). Changes included: - runtime/evacuation/kv_preserver.go: new package that orchestrates per-tenant KV snapshotting, writes compressed snapshots to temporary object storage, and signals rehydrate intents to target region agents. - routing/taper_controller.go: staged taper controller implementing a leaky-window traffic shift (configurable steps, step latency, and backoff on rehydrate failures). - runtime/evacuation/kv_preserver_test.go and tests/unit/taper_controller_test.go: unit and integration-style mocks to validate preservation and taper progression in failure scenarios. - docs/design/kv-evacuation.md: design doc describing tradeoffs, config knobs, and operational runbook for operators. - telemetry/metrics.yaml: added metrics for preservation_success_total, preservation_bytes, rehydrate_latency_ms_bucket, taper_step_progress, taper_backoff_count. Rollout plan: staged feature flag: rollout=off in main, enable for a pilot org in dedicated staging, monitor preservation_success_total and rehydrate_latency_ms for 1 week, then enable for Canary region 3. In case of increased tail latency or preservation failure rate > 2%, automatic rollback to previous behavior. Checklist: - [x] unit tests for preserver (happy/failure paths) - [x] integration mocks for cross-region rehydrate - [x] metrics + dashboards (temporary) - [x] feature flags and operator runbook - [x] e2e smoke run in staging Results: In staging Canary (region-3) we saw median rehydrate latency 45ms, 95th 210ms, preservation_success_total=98.7% over a 24h simulated evacuation. Tail latency during failover reduced by ~38% for heavy-tenant workloads compared to the previous cold-redispatch baseline. Safety and rollback: if kv_preserver reports repeated write failures to object storage, the system logs and emits preservation_fail events and disables preservation for that tenant (falls back to standard drain). The taper controller will back off and hold at the last safe step until rehydrate success or a manual operator action. Related: ENG-2129 (regional evacuation reliability), ENG-2173 (tenant cold-start regressions). Notes: This PR is intentionally conservative about the size of preserved snapshots (hot-only heuristic, LRU threshold) to limit cross-region bandwidth. The object storage used for temporary snapshots is lifecycle-managed (ttl 1h) to avoid long-tail storage costs. Follow-ups: an optimization pass to stream-preserve very large KV objects and a dedicated telemetry alert for repeated per-tenant preservation failures.
